newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Seven says library buy to speed MGM float.
newsitem.headline: Seven says library buy to speed MGM float.

text.p: Movie studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer's (MGM) US$573 million purchase of a film library and studio from the Metro-Media group would accelerate MGM's plans for a float and capital raising, MGM's part owner Seven Network Ltd said on Friday.

Seven Chairman Kerry Stokes told Reuters in an interview MGM's purchase of Orion Pictures and The Samuel Goldwyn Company would add about US$50 million to annual earnings and also help reduce overheads.
"We had always expected to have an IPO (initial public offering), but this will accelerate and bring it forward," Stokes said.
Seven said in July 1996 when it and Kirk Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp jointly bought MGM for US$1.3 billion that it wanted to float MGM within three to five years.
Stokes said Seven had no plans to sell its MGM stake in the float and was a long-term shareholder in the movie studio.
